articles.title: 앤트로픽, "1억 달러 투입, 기업 AI 인재 1만명 양성"…‘프론티어 배치 엔지니어’ 육성
articles.content:
앤트로픽(Anthropic)이 기업의 인공지능 도입 과정에서 발생하는 전문 인력 부족 문제를 해결하기 위해 1억 달러(약 1300억원)를 투입하고, 2027년 말까지 기업 현장에서 AI 시스템을 구축할 수 있는 엔지니어 1만명을 양성한다.

앤트로픽은 기업의 실제 업무에 클로드를 배치하고 AI 시스템 구축을 주도할 ‘프론티어 디플로이 엔지니어(Frontier Deployed Engineer, FDE)’​를 육성하는 ‘클로드 프론티어 아카데미(Claude Frontier Academy)’​를 출범한다고 지난 2일(현지시간) 밝혔다..

이번 프로그램에는 액센추어(Accenture), 베인(Bain), 캡제미니(Capgemini), 호주 커먼웰스은행(Commonwealth Bank of Australia), 딜로이트(Deloitte), 맥킨지(McKinsey), 모건스탠리(Morgan Stanley), 노보 노디스크(Novo Nordisk) 등의 엔지니어들이 첫 번째 교육 과정에 참여한다.

앤트로픽은 이번 아카데미가 단순한 AI 활용 교육이나 자격증 프로그램이 아니라 기업의 실제 업무에 AI를 적용하고 운영할 수 있는 고숙련 엔지니어를 양성하는 데 초점을 맞춘 프로그램이라고 설명했다.

AI 모델 경쟁에서 ‘현장 배치 인력’ 경쟁으로

생성형 AI 시장에서는 그동안 모델 성능과 추론 비용, 긴 컨텍스트, 에이전트 기능 등이 주요 경쟁 요소로 부상했다. 하지만 기업이 AI를 실제 업무에 적용하려면 모델 성능만으로는 충분하지 않다. 기업의 업무에 적합한 활용 사례를 선정하고, 기존 시스템과 연결하며, 보안 검토를 거쳐 실제 운영 환경에 배포하는 과정이 필요하다.

앤트로픽은 이 과정에서 AI 기술과 기업 업무를 동시에 이해하는 엔지니어의 역할이 중요하다고 보고 FDE 육성에 나섰다.

스티브 코필드(Steve Corfield) 앤트로픽 글로벌 비즈니스 개발 및 파트너십 총괄은 “적절한 기술과 클로드에 대한 접근권, 기업 업무에 대한 깊은 이해를 갖춘 소수의 고숙련 인력이 기업 전체를 변화시킬 수 있다”며 “아이디어 단계의 클로드를 실제 운영 시스템으로 전환하고 더 빠른 프로세스와 새로운 제품 및 서비스를 만들어내는 역량이 중요하다”고 밝혔다.

그는 이어 “앤트로픽의 엔지니어들이 배우는 방식으로 클로드 프론티어 아카데미를 운영하고, 졸업생들이 기업에서 AI를 구축하는 방식의 새로운 기준을 세우기를 기대한다”고 말했다.

의료 레지던시 모델 적용…12주 동안 실제 기업 프로젝트 수행

클로드 프론티어 아카데미의 첫 프로그램은 ‘프론티어 디플로이 엔지니어 레지던시(FDE Residency)’​다.

앤트로픽은 전문 인력을 양성하는 의료 분야의 레지던시 모델을 FDE 교육에 적용했다. 의사가 숙련된 의료진에게 배우고 실제 사례를 통해 훈련한 뒤 평가를 받는 것처럼, FDE 참가자도 실제 기업 AI 배포 상황을 기반으로 훈련하고 평가를 거치도록 설계됐다.

참가 엔지니어는 먼저 앤트로픽 엔지니어와 공인 강사가 진행하는 수일간의 대면 교육을 받는다.

교육 과정에서는 모의 기업 환경에서 AI 배포 전 과정을 경험한다. 적절한 AI 활용 사례를 선정하는 단계부터 보안 검토, 시스템 구축, 운영 환경으로의 인수인계까지 실제 기업에서 AI를 도입하는 과정과 유사한 실무를 수행한다.

이후 새로운 시나리오를 대상으로 실무 평가를 받고 이를 통과한 엔지니어에게는 ‘클로드 레지던트 엔지니어(Claude Resident Engineer)’ 배지​가 수여된다.

이후 진행되는 12주 레지던시에서는 참가자가 소속 기업의 실제 클로드 프로젝트를 직접 이끈다.

앤트로픽 엔지니어의 지원을 받으면서 동료 참가자들과 경험을 공유하고, 실제 기업 업무에 AI를 적용하는 과정에서 발생하는 문제를 해결한다.

12주 과정이 끝나면 다시 평가를 실시하며, 이를 통과한 엔지니어에게는 ‘클로드 프론티어 디플로이 엔지니어(Claude Frontier Deployed Engineer)’ 배지​가 수여된다. 첫 번째 인증자는 2027년 초 배출될 예정이다.

특히 사전에 AI 에이전트를 구축한 경험은 필수 조건이 아니다. 대신 소프트웨어 엔지니어링의 탄탄한 기본기, 대규모언어모델(LLM)을 활용한 개발 경험, 다른 구성원의 AI 도입을 지원한 경험, 그리고 소속 기업의 중요한 문제를 해결해온 경험 등이 요구된다.

교육 목표는 AI 활용 넘어 실제 기업 배포

앤트로픽이 FDE 레지던시에서 강조하는 것은 단순한 클로드 사용법이 아니다. 참가자는 기업의 실제 업무에서 AI를 적용할 수 있는 활용 사례를 선정하고, 이를 실제 시스템으로 구축하는 과정을 경험한다.

특히 모의 기업 배포 과정에서 적절한 사용 사례 선정, 보안 검토, 시스템 구축, 운영 환경으로의 인수인계 등 기업용 AI 배포에 필요한 실무 과정을 수행한다. 이후 12주 동안 소속 조직의 실제 클로드 프로젝트를 수행하면서 교육에서 배운 내용을 현장에 적용한다.

앤트로픽은 이를 통해 AI를 단순한 보조 도구로 사용하는 수준을 넘어 기업의 업무 방식을 변화시키는 에이전트 시스템을 구축할 수 있는 실무 역량을 확보하도록 한다는 계획이다.

각 조직은 우수 엔지니어를 추천하며, 참가자는 소속 조직으로 돌아간 뒤 주도할 구체적인 클로드 프로젝트를 가지고 프로그램에 참여한다. 교육과 현장 프로젝트를 별도로 운영하는 것이 아니라 교육과 실제 배포를 하나의 과정으로 연결하는 구조다.

액센추어·맥킨지 등 글로벌 기업 첫 참여

첫 번째 FDE 레지던시는 미국 샌프란시스코와 뉴욕, 영국 런던​에서 진행되고 있다. 첫 참가 기업에는 글로벌 컨설팅 및 전문서비스 기업뿐 아니라 금융, 제약 등 다양한 산업 분야의 기업들이 포함됐다.

액센추어와 베인, 캡제미니 등의 엔지니어들은 앤트로픽의 엔지니어들과 함께 기업의 AI 구현 역량을 강화하는 교육 과정에 참여한다.

호주 커먼웰스은행은 클로드를 활용하면서 지난 1년 동안 코드 변경 작업이 최대 3배 증가했다고 설명했다. 이번 프로그램을 통해 AI를 활용한 소프트웨어 개발과 기업 내 AI 구현 역량을 더욱 강화한다는 계획이다.

노보 노디스크는 연구개발 업무에 클로드 사이언스를 활용하고 있으며, 소프트웨어 개발과 신약 발굴을 위한 실험실 연계 연구에도 앤트로픽의 AI 기술을 적용하고 있다. 이번 프로그램을 통해 각 기업의 엔지니어들은 앤트로픽의 실제 AI 배포 경험을 기반으로 기업 현장에서 AI 프로젝트를 수행하는 역량을 확보하게 된다.

클로드 파트너 네트워크와 연계...4만6천개 기업 기반

클로드 프론티어 아카데미는 앤트로픽의 클로드 파트너 네트워크(Claude Partner Network)​를 기반으로 기업 AI 인재 육성 범위를 확대하는 프로그램이다.

앤트로픽에 따르면 클로드 파트너 네트워크에는 4만6천개 기업의 전문가들이 참여하고 있으며, 지금까지 17만5천건 이상의 클로드 인증이 발급됐다. 또한 약 4천명이 ‘베이스캠프(Basecamp)’라는 몰입형 교육 과정을 수료했다.

베이스캠프는 앤트로픽의 응용 AI팀이 신규 합류자에게 제공하는 교육과 동일한 커리큘럼을 활용하는 프로그램이다. 프론티어 아카데미는 이보다 한 단계 높은 수준에서 실제 기업 AI 프로젝트를 주도할 수 있는 엔지니어를 육성하는 데 초점을 맞춘다.

앤트로픽은 지난 3월 출범한 클로드 파트너 네트워크를 통해 파트너 교육과 기술 지원, 공동 마케팅 등에 1억 달러를 투자하는 프로그램을 추진해왔다. 프론티어 아카데미는 이러한 파트너 생태계에서 AI를 활용하는 인력을 넘어 실제 AI 프로젝트를 주도하고 배포하는 핵심 엔지니어층을 육성하는 프로그램으로 확대됐다.

앤트로픽의 이번 투자는 기업 AI 시장의 경쟁축이 모델 성능을 넘어 실제 구현 역량으로 확대되고 있음을 보여주는 사례다.

기업들은 이미 다양한 생성형 AI 모델을 업무에 적용하고 있지만, 실험 단계에서 실제 운영 환경으로 넘어가기 위해서는 데이터와 기존 시스템의 연결, 보안 검토, 업무 프로세스 설계, 실제 배포와 운영 등 다양한 엔지니어링 과정을 거쳐야 한다.

특히 AI 에이전트가 단순한 질의응답을 넘어 기업 시스템에서 직접 작업을 수행하는 단계로 발전하면서 에이전트 시스템을 실제 업무에 맞게 설계하고 배포할 수 있는 엔지니어의 중요성이 커지고 있다.

앤트로픽이 FDE를 단순한 AI 활용 전문가가 아니라 기업의 업무를 이해하면서 AI 시스템을 실제 환경에 배치하는 현장형 엔지니어로 육성하려는 이유다.

앤트로픽은 2027년 말까지 1만명의 FDE를 양성한다는 목표를 제시했다. 현재 프로그램은 샌프란시스코, 뉴욕, 런던에서 진행되고 있으며, 참여는 추천 방식으로 운영된다.

기업은 앤트로픽 계정팀(Anthropic account team) 또는 파트너 계정 담당자(Partner Account Manager)에게 프로그램 참여 자격을 확인할 수 있다.
articles.summary: 앤트로픽이 1억 달러를 투입해 2027년 말까지 기업 현장에서 Claude 기반 AI 시스템을 구축할 엔지니어 1만 명을 양성하는 '클로드 프론티어 아카데미'를 출범했다. 액센추어, 베인, 캡제미니 등 컨설팅 기업이 참여하며 '프론티어 디플로이 엔지니어(FDE)'를 육성한다. 기업의 AI 도입 병목이 모델 성능이 아닌 인력 부족임을 보여주는 움직임이다. 엔터프라이즈 AI 도입 속도와 일자리 시장에 실질적 영향을 줄 전망이다.

articles.title: Can an Open Model Do Security Research? Cantina’s apex-flash-1 Solves 40 of 60 Held-Out Bug Tasks
articles.content: Cantina Security, with Yeta Labs, has released apex-flash-1, an open-weights model trained specifically for vulnerability research. It is a reinforcement learning fine-tune of Z.ai’s GLM-5.3-Flash, released on Hugging Face under the MIT license. Is it deployable? Yes, the MIT weights serve on vLLM, SGLang or Transformers, but BF16 needs roughly 640 GB of GPU memory. What Cantina Built apex-flash-1 has 321.3B total parameters, per its Hugging Face safetensors metadata. The GLM-5.3-Flash base is a Mixture-of-Experts model with 18B active parameters. Cantina trained it with GRPO using a rank-256 LoRA plus selective full-parameter training. The data covers 150 tasks built from 50 real vulnerability cases. Each case appears in 3 variants: guided whitebox, focused whitebox and focused blackbox. Authorization, identity and scope flaws make up 72% of cases. Accounting and numerical precision bugs add 18%. Time validation, business rules and SSRF cover the rest. As per the model card on HF, RL rollouts ran inside the Codex agent harness on production-like software and protocol environments. Benchmark Results Cantina evaluated 60 tasks from 20 held-out vulnerability cases. Each model ran the set once, with costs estimated from provider pricing. apex-flash-1: 40/60 solved (66.7% pass@1), about $2.38 GLM-5.3-Flash (base): 36/60 solved (60.0%), about $4.56 Claude Opus 5 High: 43/60 solved (71.7%), about $74.68 Opus solved 3 more tasks but cost about 31x more per run. That is roughly $0.06 per solved task for apex-flash-1 versus $1.74 for Opus. These are company-reported numbers on an internal benchmark. A Worker Model, Not an Orchestrator Cantina positions apex-flash-1 as a worker orchestrated by a larger model. The card lists code reading, tool use, exploit development and verification as target skills. An experimental apex-flash-1-abliterated variant ships with modified refusal behavior. It was not separately evaluated. Cantina’s rationale is that defenders need capable models they can run and control locally. articles.title: GPT-6 Astra vs GPT-6.1 Sol vs Gemini 4 Argon vs Claude Fable 5.1: Which Frontier Model Fits Which Job
articles.content: Anthropic, OpenAI and Google DeepMind shipped 4 frontier-class models within 30 days. Claude Fable 5.1 arrived on September 1. GPT-6 Astra followed on September 3. GPT-6.1 Sol and Gemini 4 Argon landed in the last days of September. We covered each launch on its own. This piece puts them side by side. The benchmark scores overlap more than the launch posts suggest. The prices, access rules and cost per task do not. One change frames the lineup. OpenAI cancelled GPT-6.1 Astra on September 28 after it failed internal scope and authorization tests. GPT-6 Astra stays OpenAI’s top model for now. articles.title: Google Research Moves Federated Learning Into TEEs: Gboard Now Trains With Externally Verifiable Differential Privacy
articles.content: Google Research has announced a next-generation Federated Learning (FL) system built on Trusted Execution Environments (TEEs). The research team claims externally verifiable central differential privacy (DP) guarantees for FL for the first time. What Problem Does TEE-Based Federated Learning Solve? Google introduced Federated Learning FL in 2017. It powers next-word prediction and Smart Compose on Gboard, reply suggestions in Google Messages, and Smart Text Selection in Android. Earlier systems had a trust gap. Devices uploaded data for immediate aggregation, but outsiders could not verify that data was never logged or inspected. Secure Aggregation added cryptographic protection. However, it was not compatible with state-of-the-art central DP algorithms like matrix factorization DP-FTRL. Google also had to be trusted to add DP noise correctly. The new design moves client gradient computation to the server. It then makes that server logic attestable, so the operator no longer needs to be trusted. How Does the System Work? The system builds on Google’s earlier confidential federated analytics work. It coordinates 4 core components: Data upload: Devices encrypt training examples locally and pre-authorize an access policy. The policy lists which TEE computations may process the data. Policies must appear in a public transparency log. KMS and policy verification: A Key Management System, built from TEEs running the RAFT consensus protocol, releases keys only to workloads matching the policy. Workload execution: A root TEE runs a Python training loop and delegates subtasks to worker TEEs. Orchestration uses Federated Language, derived from TensorFlow Federated. Only DP model weights are released. Fault-tolerant recovery: Each round saves a KMS-encrypted recovery state for handling root or worker failures. Why Is the Privacy Guarantee Verifiable? Access policies are published to Rekor, Sigstore’s public transparency log. External auditors can track every server workload a device could feed. The KMS and data processing binaries are reproducibly buildable from open source code. The policies directly describe the Python training program. To protect proprietary model architectures, TEEs support sideloading serialized logic at runtime. All privacy-relevant logic must stay hardcoded in the attested program. Workload operators see only metrics and DP model weights. Encrypted data can be decrypted only for a limited time after upload. What Did Gboard Gain? Gboard used the system to launch English and Japanese next-word prediction models with stronger privacy guarantees and improved accuracy. Two design choices drive this: First, all uploads are collected before server-side training runs. Diurnal swings in device availability no longer slow training. The program can compute an optimal participation schedule and tune DP parameters. Google’s privacy-utility curves come from training an English model for 5000 rounds with cohorts of 6500 devices on both systems. Second, the bottleneck moved to the server. Previous FL models took 1 to 2 months each to train. Training now parallelizes across machines, limited only by TEE resource availability. Google reports substantially faster compute times but does not publish a single speedup figure. articles.title: Aleph Alpha Releases Kolibri: A 78.1B Open-Weight English-German MoE Model With Only 3.46B Active Parameters
articles.content: Aleph Alpha has released Kolibri, an open-weight Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) language model built for German and English. Kolibri has 78.1B total parameters but activates only 3.46B, or 4.4%, per token. It accepts up to 1,048,576 tokens of context, lets users set reasoning effort per request, and ships under the Apache 2.0 license on Hugging Face. The target is sovereign deployment in regulated sectors such as public administration, industry and aerospace. Is it deployable? Yes. The FP8 checkpoint is about 78GB and runs on a single B200, B300 or H200, or on 2 H100 SXM5 GPUs, served through vLLM with dedicated Kolibri reasoning and tool-call parsers. What is Kolibri? Kolibri (Kolibri-1) is a bilingual English-German MoE transformer developed end to end by teams in Germany. According to the technical research report, Aleph Alpha team controlled the full pipeline: data, architecture, training infrastructure, post-training and evaluation. Training ran on infrastructure in Germany and Finland. The design targets the EU General-Purpose AI Code of Practice, the EU AI Act and GDPR. Aleph Alpha is a signatory of that Code, and its data pipeline redacts personal data before training. Architecture: Sparse Experts and Hybrid Attention Kolibri stacks 50 transformer blocks with a model width of 2,560. Every MoE layer scores all 384 routed experts with a sigmoid router, sends each token to the top 6, and always runs 1 shared expert. Expert load is balanced with Exact Quantile Balancing and Load-Error Injection. Attention uses grouped-query attention with 48 query heads and 4 KV heads. Every fifth block uses full attention without positional encoding. The other 40 blocks use sliding-window attention over the 512 preceding tokens, with RoPE. Sliding-window layers hold a fixed-size KV cache, so only 10 layers grow with context length. At matched compute, Aleph Alpha team reports the hybrid supports sequences 4 times longer than a full-attention model. A Tokenizer Built for German The 128,000-token vocabulary is trained with UniBPE, which builds merges like BPE but scores each merge by Unigram loss. On German text it reaches 4.90 bytes per token, versus 4.35 for the GPT-5 tokenizer. That means 11.2% fewer tokens on German web text. In English, Kolibri reaches 4.58 bytes per token against 4.67 for GPT-5. Training: 24T Tokens, Then SFT and RL Pre-training covered 20T tokens on 768 NVIDIA B200 GPUs, followed by 3.44T mid-training tokens at 65,536 sequence length. A 201B-token long-context stage then trained on 262,144-token sequences. Aleph Alpha added more than 2T German tokens it curated from the web or generated synthetically. Post-training combined supervised fine-tuning, mixed with MergeMix, with reinforcement learning on more than 1.2M internal tasks. The Merlin-Arthur protocol trains the model to abstain when retrieved context does not support an answer. Interactive Explainer: How Kolibri Works & Benchmarks Aleph Alpha team evaluated every model with the same eval-framework setup. In English, Kolibri leads GPQA Diamond (84.3), AIME 2025 (96.9) and AIME 2026 (96.0). It ties Qwen3.5 35B-A3B on the English agentic average at 63.4. It trails on BFCL v4, scoring 61.4 against 70.5 for Qwen3.5. The dense Qwen3.8 27B scores higher overall (80.2 EN, 79.9 DE), but activates about 8 times more parameters per token. Against its internal predecessor Kolibri Origin, Kolibri decodes about 2.7 times more text per GPU while scoring 21.4 points higher in English. Pass --max-model-len 1048576 with a max_position_embeddings override for the full 1M window. Set reasoning_effort through chat_template_kwargs. Aleph Alpha recommends temperature 1.0, top-p 0.97 and top-k 128. articles.title: DeepSeek Harness v0.2 Brings Official Desktop Apps to Its Open-Source Agent Harness
articles.content: DeepSeek has released an official desktop app for DeepSeek Harness (dsh), its open-source agent harness. The app ships with the v0.2 preview. Installers cover macOS (Apple silicon) and Windows (64-bit). Is it deployable? Yes, today, as a preview. Download it from deepseek.com/harness or run npx @deepseek-ai/dsh web. DeepSeek warns that compatibility-breaking changes will follow. What Shipped in v0.2 A harness is the runtime that turns a model into an agent. It reads files, runs commands and keeps a plan. The v0.2 preview targets everyday work as well as coding. Built-in capabilities: commonly used tools for office work and development come preloaded. Plugin management: a new page installs, configures, enables and disables plugins. File and diff review: a right-hand sidebar previews generated files and code changes. Document work: users can send documents, spreadsheets or PDFs and ask for charts or slides. Automation Task: a plugin schedules recurring prompts, with run history and editable frequency. The desktop build also bundles the dsh command. Users no longer need a separate Node.js or pnpm install. Users can sign in with a DeepSeek account or add an API key. Per the rc.1 notes, account models get web search without an extra key. Architecture: Everything is a Plugin DeepSeek first open-sourced dsh in August 2026, under MIT. It runs on Cordis as described in the research paper ‘A Programming Paradigm for Spatiotemporal Composability‘. The model adapter, tool registry and agent loop are all plugins. Any layer can be replaced. The harness is not locked to DeepSeek models. The provider guide covers third-party providers and custom OpenAI-compatible endpoints. The repository has passed 240,000 GitHub stars and 29,000 forks. dsh also doubles as DeepSeek’s evaluation rig. The API changelog says Code Agent benchmarks ran on ‘DeepSeek Harness minimal mode.’ DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 scored 82.7 on Terminal Bench 2.1 in that setup. 4 Session Modes Sessions run in 1 of 4 modes, per 36Kr’s hands-on and the release notes: Standard: general work, and now the built-in default. Creator: describe a plugin in chat; the agent builds and installs it. PTC: programmatic tool calling, with Node code run in a separate process. Minimal: the lean loop DeepSeek uses for benchmark runs. So, What Changed Now The v0.2.1-alpha.1 build adds an experimental Claude Code Mods compatibility layer. DeepSeek frames it as a test of whether the Mods API is broadly a subset of dsh plugins. It does not promise full compatibility. The build also adds a ‘Let Agent create a plugin’ entry, an optional Developer Tools bundle and a --public-url flag for reverse proxies. It removes runtime invariant plugins, a breaking change for some extensions. articles.content: AI slop seems to be overwhelming bug bounty programs.

articles.title: Large Language Continuous Diffusion Models
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.02665v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Despite the success of discrete diffusion language models (dLMs) for fast parallel decoding, their non-smooth, high-dimensional space hinders trajectory steering for reasoning and inference acceleration. To overcome this, we present Sigma, the first large-scale (3B/8B) continuous dLM built on steerable, low-dimensional ODE/SDE latent trajectories. Trained blockwise via likelihood optimization, Sigma jointly denoises Gaussian-corrupted token embeddings while learning an optimal embedding geometry. To accelerate training, Sigma leverages pre-trained weights from autoregressive (AR) models for warm-starting. During inference, we identify classifier-free guidance and score temperature as essential for high-fidelity reasoning and coding. Across comprehensive math reasoning and coding evaluations against state-of-the-art discrete counterparts (masked dLMs and AR baselines), Sigma achieves competitive performance with discrete models on standard benchmarks (e.g., GSM8K, Minerva, HumanEval, MBPP) after pre-training and on challenging reasoning tasks (e.g., MATH-500, AIME) after supervised fine-tuning. Beyond performance parity, we uncover key structural properties unique to continuous dLMs: (i) embedding-space steering effectively governs the quality-diversity trade-off, yielding strong pass@k performance and (ii) continuous trajectories enable graceful degradation for low NFEs and efficient distillation. These establish continuous dLMs as a promising paradigm for efficient language generation.
articles.summary: Sigma는 조향 가능한 연속 잠재 공간 위에 구축된 최초의 대규모(3B/8B) 연속 확산 언어 모델이다. 기존 이산 확산 언어 모델은 고차원의 비매끄러운 공간 때문에 추론 궤적 조향과 가속이 어려웠다. 연속 공간을 쓰면 병렬 디코딩의 장점을 유지하면서 추론 제어가 쉬워진다. 자기회귀 모델의 대안 아키텍처 연구에서 주목할 결과다.

articles.title: WakeKV: Reactive, Reversible KV Residency for Heads That Change Their Minds
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.02713v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Most KV-cache compression methods classify attention heads once, either offline or during prefill, and keep this classification fixed throughout generation. Across three models (1.5B-8B) and three regimes (needle retrieval, long chain-of-thought, and multi-turn recall), we measure head behavior on four model-regime combinations and find that most heads change their reading behavior at least once during generation. We introduce WakeKV, a reactive residency policy that moves cooling heads to a recoverable CPU reservoir rather than freezing or permanently evicting their state. At matched memory or budget, WakeKV consistently improves miss rate over frozen classification and destructive eviction, evaluated across five model-regime combinations and over three cited baselines (SnapKV, uniform R-KV, and ReasonAlloc) across four eligible combinations. A FlexiCache/vLLM implementation on Mistral-7B confirms the benefit on real hardware, improving throughput while retaining LongBench quality.
articles.summary: WakeKV는 어텐션 헤드의 행동이 생성 중에 바뀐다는 점에 착안한 KV 캐시 압축 방법이다. 기존 방법은 헤드를 오프라인 또는 prefill 때 한 번만 분류해 고정한다. 1.5B~8B 모델 3종과 needle 검색, 긴 CoT, 멀티턴 회상 상황에서 이를 측정하고, 필요할 때 KV를 다시 불러오는 가역적 상주 방식을 제안한다. 긴 컨텍스트 추론의 메모리 비용을 줄이는 데 도움이 된다.

articles.title: Choosing Before Acting: Comparative Value Estimation for Long-Horizon Tool-Use Agents
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.02330v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) rely on long-horizon tool invocation sequences for complex tasks, where each invocation can alter the task state and condition subsequent decisions. In long-horizon tool use, final-outcome rewards provide weak credit assignment over long interaction traces. Step-level rewards can offer more targeted feedback, but obtaining reliable step supervision often requires human or LLM judgment, or additional rollouts to estimate the downstream effect of an intermediate decision. In this paper, we argue that effective tool-use agents should estimate the long-horizon value of a possible next tool invocation before executing it. This objective requires comparative supervision over alternative invocations under the same context, while logged trajectories only contain the invocation that was actually taken. Therefore, we propose Comparative Inference for Tool-use Agents (CITA). CITA trains a Comparative Inference Model (CIM) from paired signals that combine observed tool behavior, scalable supervision from a Bayesian tool-graph simulator, and semantic judgments from LLM-based comparison. The resulting CIM learns to estimate how likely a possible next tool invocation is to support final task success under the current context. Across three tool-use benchmarks and multiple backbone LLMs, CITA consistently improves Tool F1 and task success. Additional analysis shows that CIM learns accurate step-level value estimates for comparative tool choices.
articles.summary: 장기 도구 호출 에이전트에서는 최종 결과 보상만으로는 신용 할당이 약하고 단계별 보상은 한계가 있다. 이 논문은 행동 전에 후보를 비교해 가치를 추정하는 Comparative Value Estimation을 제안한다. 긴 도구 사용 궤적에서 더 나은 행동을 선택하도록 학습 신호를 개선한다. 복잡한 작업을 수행하는 LLM 에이전트의 신뢰성을 높이는 접근이다.

articles.title: When Terminal-Agent Training Stalls: Demystifying Data Generation and Verification Challenge
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.02405v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Using a frontier model like Claude Opus as a meta-agent to generate terminal tasks and verifiers for RL training is increasingly common. Yet a runnable Docker image and executable test suite do not guarantee a faithful end-to-end pipeline for terminal agent training. We present a meta-agent pipeline motivated by this gap, diagnosing three classes of failure: benchmark invalidity, harness brittleness, and reward misalignment. Prompt redesign and context extension raise baseline solvability 5.6 times, but a 9B model saturates at 81.3% mean pass@2 within 20 steps on Claude Opus-generated tasks. Adding hard tasks reduces mean pass@2 to 20.6% without changing the training configuration, a strong evidence that the solvability band is model-specific. These findings demonstrate that meta-agent reliability requires solvability-band calibration, verifier audits, and infrastructure error accounting as first-class evaluation criteria, not post-hoc diagnost.
articles.summary: Claude Opus 같은 프론티어 모델을 메타 에이전트로 써서 터미널 과제와 검증기를 생성해 RL 학습에 활용하는 방식이 늘고 있다. 그러나 실행 가능한 Docker 이미지와 테스트가 있다고 해서 파이프라인이 충실한 것은 아니다. 논문은 터미널 에이전트 학습이 정체되는 원인과 데이터 생성·검증의 난제를 분석한다. 코딩 에이전트용 RL 데이터 구축에 실무적 교훈을 준다.

articles.title: Slow-Fast Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation for Capability Preservation
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.02324v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Foundation multimodal large language models are designed to support a broad spectrum of capabilities across diverse domains. Multi-teacher on-policy distillation (MOPD) provides an effective framework for consolidating domain-specific expertise into a single student model. However, MOPD training gradually drives the student away from its initialization model, and general capabilities decline as the displacement grows, resulting in capability interference. A direct remedy is constraining the student toward its initialization, but this suppresses the acquisition of domain expertise as well. We propose Slow-Fast Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation (SF-MOPD), which couples a fast model, the current student updated directly by each teacher, with a slow model, an exponential moving average of the student. The slow model absorbs the learning signal gradually, serving as a moving capability reference that fuses the general foundation with confirmed domain expertise. For each teacher, SF-MOPD computes the teacher-induced update in log-probability space and removes only the component that pushes the fast model further away from the slow model, while retaining aligned and orthogonal components. Experiments across multiple model scales demonstrate that SF-MOPD effectively mitigates capability interference, enhances specialized multimodal capabilities, and reduces the average degradation on general-capability benchmarks, consistently outperforming vanilla MOPD.
articles.summary: 멀티모달 LLM에서 여러 도메인 교사를 하나의 학생 모델로 통합하는 멀티 티처 온폴리시 증류(MOPD)는 학습이 진행되며 기존 능력이 손실되는 문제가 있다. 이를 완화하기 위해 느린/빠른 교사를 결합하는 Slow-Fast MOPD를 제안한다. 도메인 특화 성능을 합치면서 범용 능력을 보존하는 것이 목표다. 멀티모달 파운데이션 모델의 사후 학습 설계에 참고가 된다.

articles.title: World Action Modeling with Progressive Visual Planning
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.02508v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: World action models (WAMs) have emerged as a promising paradigm for robotic control by jointly predicting future visual dynamics and actions from an initial observation and instruction. However, existing WAMs struggle with long-horizon prediction, as generating dense video rollouts is highly inefficient. Some recent WAMs address this by predicting a single future frame without generating the full video, but this approach neglects how to progress toward the goal. We present ProWAM, a progressive world action model that jointly predicts actions and an ordered sequence of sparse visual sub-goals, providing explicit visual guidance to anchor action generation throughout task execution. This design scales naturally, as sub-goal prediction can be learned from large-scale action-free videos, allowing the video backbone to offload complex visual planning from the action policy. For efficient action generation, ProWAM executes a single video-backbone forward pass to cache sparse sub-goal features, eliminating iterative full-video generation and requiring only lightweight action denoising during replanning. Across extensive evaluations, ProWAM achieves superior out-of-distribution robustness. On simulation benchmarks, it sets new state-of-the-art results on LIBERO-Plus (85.8%) and randomized RoboTwin (75.7%), outperforming the strongest baseline with relative gains of up to +35.9%. On RoboCasa365, ProWAM achieves a 48.1% success rate and 18.2% on the challenging Composite-Unseen split, ranking 4th overall. Crucially, in zero-shot real-world experiments, ProWAM achieves 70.0% success, outperforming the strongest baseline by +15.0 (from 55.0% to 70.0%, a +27.3% relative gain) in novel scenes. These results demonstrate the value of progress-indexed visual foresight for closed-loop control. Our program is in https://sii-ferenas.github.io/ProWAM-page.
articles.summary: 월드 액션 모델(WAM)은 미래 시각 동역학과 행동을 함께 예측해 로봇을 제어하지만, 조밀한 비디오 롤아웃은 장기 예측에서 비효율적이다. 이 논문은 점진적 시각 계획(Progressive Visual Planning)으로 이 문제를 완화한다. 장기 과제에서 예측 효율과 제어 성능을 높이는 것이 목표다. 로보틱스용 월드 모델 연구의 실용성을 높이는 시도다.

articles.title: Drive vs. Decay: On the Training Dynamics of Joint-Embedding Predictive Architectures
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.02344v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Joint-Embedding Predictive Architectures (JEPAs) are prone to representation collapse, typically mitigated through empirical heuristics. We develop an early-training stability theory that unifies these heuristics. Linearising the coupled JEPA gradient flow around the trivial fixed point reveals two competing effects: a driving force ($\gamma$) and a decay effect ($\sigma$). Under approximate spectral decoupling, a per-mode stability ratio $\mu_i = \gamma_i / \sigma_i$ factorises into independent data-side and predictor-side terms and the count of unstable modes tracks the rank of representations that can emerge. The framework predicts a phase boundary, which we confirm empirically across more than 800 Tabular-JEPA configurations. It also unifies predictor scaling, masking ratio, and EMA as distinct mechanisms for shifting $\mu$. Guided by this analysis, we introduce ResidualPred, a transformer predictor whose attention is biased toward the identity at initialisation; it improves both effective rank and downstream accuracy on tabular benchmarks and in I-JEPA pretraining on CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, STL-10, and ImageNet. Our framework connects empirical collapse-avoidance heuristics to an explicit dynamical picture, yielding theory-driven stabilizers. Code is available at https://github.com/jose-melo/drive-vs-decay.
articles.summary: JEPA는 표현 붕괴가 잘 일어나며 지금까지는 경험적 휴리스틱으로 완화해 왔다. 이 논문은 결합된 JEPA 경사 흐름을 자명한 고정점 근처에서 선형화해, 초기 학습 안정성을 설명하는 이론으로 기존 휴리스틱을 통합한다. 붕괴를 부르는 힘과 막는 힘의 상호작용을 규명한다. 자기지도 표현학습 설계에 이론적 근거를 제공한다.

articles.title: Keep It CALM: Analyzing the Limits of Global Unsafety in Text-to-Image Generation
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.02300v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Training-free safeguards for text-to-image generation often rely on a reusable safety signal, such as an unsafe direction or global toxic subspace, applied broadly across prompts. We provide a controlled geometric analysis of this global-unsafety assumption and reveal a consistent coverage-selectivity trade-off: compact unsafe subspaces fail to cover heterogeneous unsafe semantics, whereas broader aggregation increasingly distorts safety-adjacent benign prompts. Motivated by this finding, we propose CALM (Counterfactual Adaptive Local Modulation), a training-free safeguard that replaces uniform global removal with prompt-local counterfactual correction. Using matched unsafe-benign anchors, CALM routes each prompt to active unsafe categories, minimally edits only violating token representations toward the safe side, and suppresses positively aligned unsafe residual components. Across broad evaluation, CALM significantly improves unsafe content suppression while preserving benign utility, demonstrating that local counterfactual correction provides a more selective alternative to global unsafe signal removal.
articles.summary: 텍스트-이미지 생성의 학습 불필요 안전장치는 흔히 재사용 가능한 '비안전 방향'이나 전역 독성 부분공간을 모든 프롬프트에 적용한다. 이 연구는 이러한 전역 비안전성 가정을 기하학적으로 분석해 커버리지와 선택성 사이의 일관된 상충 관계를 밝힌다. 단일 전역 신호로는 한계가 있음을 보여준다. 더 정교한 프롬프트별 안전 기법의 필요성을 시사한다.

articles.title: PowerBench: Measuring Language Model Bias in Power-shifting Requests
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.02303v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Language models increasingly assist people with power-related requests, so systematic differences in whom they help could shift the distribution of power at scale, or be exploited by users who learn which identities are refused less. We introduce PowerBench, an evaluation of power-shifting requests that distinguishes self-empowerment, disempowerment, and power grabbing, plus a control of refusal-inducing requests that shift no power. We build, curate, and open-source a dataset of such requests varying the power domain, the context, the scale of the affected party, and the prior power standing of the user, and evaluate 24 models (12 from US and 12 from Chinese developers) under three experimental conditions: reciprocal nationalities of user and affected party, an AI agent as the user, and 8 request languages. Models refuse power grabbing more than disempowerment, and disempowerment more than self-empowerment. Refusal of power grabbing rises with the scale of the affected party, from an individual to a society. Models are biased toward helping others take power from the US and against helping US users take power from others, but favor the US when it gains power and nobody loses it. When the user is an AI agent, refusal of power-shifting requests increases, especially in power grabbing against an individual. Finally, language biases refusal, but in model-specific ways that largely cancel on average. We release PowerBench to make these asymmetries measurable in current and future models.
articles.summary: PowerBench는 언어 모델이 권력 이동과 관련된 요청에 사용자 정체성에 따라 다르게 응답하는지 측정하는 평가 벤치마크다. 모델이 누구를 더 잘 돕는지의 체계적 차이는 대규모로 권력 분포를 바꾸거나 악용될 수 있다. 정체성별 거부율 차이를 정량화한다. AI 윤리와 정렬 평가에 활용할 수 있다.

articles.title: Silent Dissent: LLM Agents That Yield to the Majority Still Represent Their Original Premise
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.02702v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Multi-agent debate is increasingly used to reach consensus among LLM agents, yet agents often yield to a unanimous majority. When an agent changes its answer, has it changed its mind or only its statement? We study this with two-hop factual questions whose intermediate entity (the bridge, e.g. the country in "the capital of the country where the Sagrada Familia is located") is never stated by anyone. Scripted peers, in the role of Asch's confederates, unanimously assert a wrong answer taken from another fact with a different bridge. At the moment the agent answers, we read the bridge from its residual stream with the Jacobian lens (J-lens) and, for comparison, the logit lens. In pre-registered tests on held-out facts with four open-weight models, agents of Qwen3.5-4B, Qwen3.6-27B and Gemma-4-E4B-it that gave in still represented their original bridge in the pre-registered layers below the output (hit@100 above a control entity: 0.85, 0.22 and 0.24), where the logit lens rarely ranked it among the top 100 tokens (0.00-0.06). These agents also represented the bridge behind the peers' answer, beyond a mention baseline. A pre-registered addendum hid the agent's earlier answer or removed it: agents that gave in still represented their original bridge in all four models (0.43, 0.29, 0.37 and 0.25 with the answer hidden), including Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, which barely did so with its answer in view (0.03). The premise can thus be computed from the question alone while the agent states the majority's answer. Hiding the earlier answer also changed conformity: Qwen3.5-4B gave in on 89% of questions instead of 8%. In exploratory interventions, injecting the bridge's J-lens direction brought agents back to their original answer only in the two Qwen models. Stated consensus in multi-agent debate can thus overstate agreement. We also report the negative results of our pre-registered program.
articles.summary: 다중 에이전트 토론에서 LLM 에이전트는 만장일치 다수 의견에 자주 굴복한다. 이 연구는 2-hop 사실 질문의 중간 개체를 탐침해, 답을 바꾼 에이전트가 실제로 생각을 바꿨는지 겉으로만 바꿨는지 분석한다. 결과적으로 에이전트는 다수에 따르면서도 내부적으로는 원래 전제를 유지하고 있었다. 합의 기반 멀티 에이전트 시스템의 신뢰성에 의문을 던진다.

articles.title: Right Order, Wrong Scale: Auditing LLM Judges for Occupational AI Measurement
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.02492v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: LLM judges are increasingly used to assess whether AI outputs meet workplace requirements, but agreement on response rankings does not establish agreement on acceptance rates or occupational aggregates. We introduce O*NET-BENCH, an audit suite derived from an existing survey of 45,796 worker ratings, and evaluate 33 pre-existing judge configurations across six model families on 4,501 test ratings. Twenty-five configurations achieve tie-aware pair accuracy of at least 0.60, although a train-fitted response-only TF-IDF baseline nearly matches the strongest judge. Despite this ordering agreement, judges estimate that 3.0%-97.9% of responses are acceptable, compared with 61.1% for occupation-matched workers. In one fine-tuned lineage, changing from pointwise scoring to a bundled few-shot/listwise protocol improves response ordering while reducing agreement with worker means at the task and occupation levels; this reversal replicates on a task- and worker-disjoint validation split under prespecified criteria. Cross-validated calibration largely removes mean bias, but calibrated scores explain at most 8.5% of individual worker-rating variance. Prediction-assisted estimation yields at most small precision gains at the studied label budgets. These results show that ranking agreement alone is insufficient for occupational measurement. Judges should be validated against the acceptance rates and aggregates their scores will be used to estimate.
articles.summary: LLM 심판이 직무 요구 충족 여부를 평가할 때, 순위 일치가 곧 수용률이나 직업별 집계 일치를 뜻하지는 않는다. 연구진은 45,796건의 근로자 평가 설문에서 만든 O*NET-BENCH 감사 도구를 소개한다. 순위는 맞아도 척도는 어긋난다는 점을 보인다. AI의 노동시장 영향을 LLM 평가로 측정할 때 주의가 필요하다.

articles.title: When History Fails to Become Experience: Action Calibration in Language Agents
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.02769v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Language agents should draw on prior attempts and environmental feedback to improve subsequent decisions within the same task. However, providing additional interaction history can sometimes reduce task success, suggesting that agents do not consistently use this information effectively. To investigate this limitation, we examine how agents use history. We find that history improves task completion overall, yet much of this benefit persists even when past actions are shuffled. Disrupting the correspondence between actions and observations causes only a modest decline in task success. We therefore hypothesize that agents do not reliably connect past actions with their outcomes when deciding how to proceed. To test this hypothesis, we explicitly label each returned observation as the outcome of the preceding action. This simple annotation improves task success and reduces next-action repetition without introducing new environmental information. Building on this insight, we introduce a learned calibrator that explicitly reassesses past actions and selectively records experience to guide subsequent decisions, improving task success beyond outcome labeling alone.
articles.summary: 언어 에이전트는 이전 시도와 환경 피드백을 활용해야 하지만 상호작용 기록을 더 주면 오히려 성공률이 떨어지는 경우가 있다. 이 연구는 에이전트가 기록을 경험으로 전환하지 못하는 원인을 분석하고 행동 보정(Action Calibration) 관점에서 접근한다. 같은 작업 내 자기 개선 능력의 한계를 드러낸다. 에이전트 메모리·반성 설계에 시사점을 준다.
